questions.q: What three things should a resume bullet for this project include, per the lesson?
options: The real architecture, a before/after outcome, and proof of production maturity (e.g. CI/CD, IAM, DR)
Only a list of every AWS service used, with no other detail
Just the word 'AWS' and the job title applied for
A promise that the pipeline has zero possible downtime
questions.explain: The lesson's example bullet names the architecture, states a concrete before/after outcome, and calls out CI/CD, least-privilege IAM, and a documented DR plan as production-maturity proof.

questions.q: What does the portfolio write-up structure recommended in this lesson mirror?
options: The five-beat story arc from Lesson 14: Business Problem, Architecture, Build, Production Practices, Results
A random ordering of AWS service names
Only the code files, with no narrative structure at all
A chronological list of every AWS console click made during the build
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly maps the portfolio document's sections onto the same five-beat arc used for presenting the project.

questions.q: Why can the interview question 'Why Redshift Serverless instead of a provisioned cluster?' be answered with a specific, defensible answer?
options: Because it traces back to a real decision made in Lesson 6, tied to Northfield's bursty, month-end-heavy query pattern
Because Redshift Serverless is always cheaper regardless of workload, with no reasoning needed
Because the question has no good answer and should be deflected
Because provisioned clusters are no longer available on AWS
questions.explain: Every question in the bank traces to an actual decision made earlier in the course — here, Northfield's bursty query pattern from Lesson 6.

questions.q: What two stages of the AWS Data Engineer career path does completing this lesson close out?
options: The Job Ready stage (AWS Fundamentals + AWS Data Engineering) and the Advanced stage (this capstone)
Only the Advanced stage — Job Ready was already separately completed elsewhere
There is only one stage in this career path
The Beginner stage and the Expert stage
questions.explain: The lesson states this closes both the Job Ready stage (individual AWS services) and the Advanced stage (this capstone, assembling them into one project).

questions.q: According to this final lesson, what two things does a student now have, having completed the whole AWS Data Engineer path?
options: Fluency with individual AWS services, and a finished, defensible project built with them
A certificate of completion and nothing else demonstrable
Only theoretical knowledge with no built project
A finished project but no understanding of the individual services behind it
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that the student now has both halves an interview tests: service fluency and a real, defensible project.
